static_traits.name: Li Beining
static_traits.social_status: Social support is limited; occasionally chats with a few acquaintances, but finds it hard to build deep friendships
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, steady tone, reporting slight anxiety during the session

basic_info.main_problem: Because my parents are strict and I lack social life, I feel like a recluse, chronically feeling isolated and lonely; these feelings began in adolescence and intensified after my parents tightened restrictions on socializing with friends. The problem worsened with age; I feel I have no real friends; it appears almost daily, especially when seeing peers socialize freely.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize loneliness and the sense of isolation are negatively affecting my mental health and overall well-being, so I am seeking counseling, hoping to lessen these effects and improve my social situation.
growth_experiences: Starting in adolescence, my parents were very protective with strict rules on going out and seeing friends, limiting social opportunities; as I grew older, these rules were not yet noticeably relaxed, and I gradually felt I cannot connect with people and have no true friends. The long-term loneliness and restricted experience mean I rarely go out for activities in daily life, my diet became irregular (sometimes skipping meals), and interpersonal relationships are mostly small talk with acquaintances, lacking deep communication.

core_beliefs: I am a person cut off from society
No one will want to be friends with me

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot socialize freely like my peers, it means I am unpopular and doomed to loneliness.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces going out, avoids initiating contact, stays at home as much as possible to avoid being compared and rejected.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot possibly have true friends.

special_situations.event: Parents enforce strict rules on outings and friendships
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: My parents' rules determine my social fate; I have almost no room for autonomous choice.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Complying with the rules, not proposing social plans to avoid conflict.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My social life is entirely decided by my parents; I am powerless.

special_situations.event: Being told 'not understood' when communicating social needs with parents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my parents do not understand me, then no one will understand me or support my socializing.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing expression of deeper needs and lowering the frequency of discussing conflict topics.

special_situations.event: Getting ready to go out or trying to make new friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my social experience is insufficient or I am not attractive enough, others will reject me.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Only engages in shallow small talk with acquaintances, avoiding deep interaction or proactive invitations.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No one will want to be friends with me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to socialize freely, to be accepted and understood by peers
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and not being understood; fearing conflict or criticism from defying parents
defense_goal: Maintains safety and family harmony by obeying parents and reducing going out
Weakening expression of deep social needs to lower the risk of being negated

object_relations.self_representation: A restricted and isolated child / recluse

object_relations.object_representation: Others are a group that might reject them

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing parents' strictness and their motives
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to understand parents as 'doing it for my own good', to dilute one's own anger and need for autonomy
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States in a gentle, tactful tone, emphasizes her parents' good intentions, reduces emotional vocabulary, avoids directly accusing control.

manifestations: Long feeling like a recluse, socially isolated
Feeling lonely and isolated almost daily, especially when seeing peers socialize freely
With acquaintances, stays only at shallow small talk, hard to share deep feelings
outcomes: Social avoidance and declining life engagement
Irregular diet, decreased quality of life

manifestations: Parents restrict going out and making friends, social autonomy defined by rules
Expressed needs not yet understood, experiencing restricted choices and helplessness

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Evaluating oneself with self-denial statements in session (such as 'no one will want to be friends with me')
Expresses willingness to try but emphasizes 'feeling stuck', proceeds cautiously
The tendency to be unwilling to share deep feelings with acquaintances repeatedly appearing in session narratives

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assuming others will reject oneself before socializing, attributing others' possible attitudes to them (such as 'no one will want to be friends with me')

exception_events.target_problem: In social situations, the client usually avoids going out due to parents' strict rules and self-denial, finding it hard to build friendships with others.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few times going out and talking with acquaintances, experiencing ease and pleasure, not withdrawing as usual.
exception_events.reason: Clues: safer environment with acquaintances present, less parental intervention at the time (or rules not yet triggered), and small willing steps that lowered anxiety.

positive_force: Occasionally has a few acquaintances providing low-intensity social opportunities
Able to notice loneliness's effects on body and mind and actively seek help
Willing to try increasing social contact in small steps and to self-monitor
negative_force: Parents' strict social rules and strong sense of external control
Self-labeling and overgeneralization (generalizing an isolated experience into a universal truth)
Mind-reading and negative anticipation before socializing (believing others will not accept)
Long-term avoidance leading to insufficient social skills and confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance and reduced going out
antecedent: Parents' strict restrictions on going out and making friends
The thought 'no one will want to be friends with me' arising when preparing to socialize
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being rejected and not being understood; the helplessness formed under parents' strict control.
target_behavior.function: Avoids possible negative evaluation and conflict, maintaining short-term safety and stability.
target_behavior.consequence: Further isolation, difficulty building friendships and participating in activities, continued unemployment and restricted life.

target_behavior.core_reason: Loneliness and low mood reducing attention to and drive for self-care, eating neglected.
target_behavior.function: Briefly avoiding inner discomfort or reducing attention to negative emotions.
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient nutritional intake, impaired physical condition and quality of life.
